items.title: Wycliffe Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001
items.q: I recently did a film score for a silent film that was done in ’25 by Oscar Micheau, called “Body and Soul.”

ctx.x: Good. I’m glad actually. What’s in the near future for you? You’ve got your own group on and off? Is it a thing that you have trouble keeping together or just as the opportunities present themselves?

I will go with the latter. I mean just as opportunities present themselves. I haven’t desired it yet that I wanted to work full time on the road with a band, the Wycliffe Gordon Quartet, Quintet, Sextet, Septet, Big Band. I don’t know. Right now I’m composing a lot. I recently did a film score for a silent film that was done in ’25 by Oscar Micheau, called “Body and Soul.” I want to do that. What’s on the burner for me? I’d like to do everything in music, whether I ever get an award for it or not doesn’t matter,…

music. So if I don’t hear it — it doesn’t have to be played on National Public Radio, it can just be played in my living room. But I’d like to be able to hear everything that I’ve written, get it out of here, on the paper, and maybe get the music performed. I think I’ll always be into teaching. I’m presently teaching at Michigan State and will be involved with the new jazz program at Juilliard that’s starting in the fall of 2001. I love to play and to perform but I love to write.
